outputs.justify_why_test_is_missing: Panel F shows normalized area across multiple exposure times with individual paired measurements (n=5 cells). To support claims about exposure-dependent changes and to quantify significance, an appropriate statistical test (e.g., repeated-measures ANOVA or a nonparametric equivalent such as Friedman test, with post-hoc multiple-comparison correction) should be reported. The current figure only shows mean±s.e.m. and fits but no p-values or test description, so readers cannot assess statistical significance or the robustness of observed trends.

Panel G displays normalized roundness across multiple exposure times with repeated measurements (n=5). Claims about changes in roundness with exposure time require statistical testing (e.g., repeated-measures ANOVA or Friedman test with appropriate post-hoc tests and multiple-comparison correction) because observations are paired within cells and there are many exposure-time groups. The caption does not report any such test, so statistical significance of the trend is not established.

Panel H shows normalized length versus exposure time (n=5, paired measurements). To support conclusions about exposure-dependent effects on length, an appropriate repeated-measures statistical analysis (or nonparametric equivalent) and multiple-comparisons correction should be reported. No test or p-values are given in the caption, so the significance of observed changes is not documented.
